title: Instant speciation by polyploidy
caption: If meiosis fails, a plant can make gametes with a double set of chromosomes. Two of them fuse to give a tetraploid offspring that cannot breed with its diploid parents, so a new species appears within one generation and without any geographic barrier.
alt: Four boxes in order: a diploid species, failed meiosis giving diploid gametes, fusion into a tetraploid offspring, and a new species.
description: Diploid species: parents with two sets of chromosomes (2n).
Failed meiosis: gametes with a double set (2n) instead of a single set.
Fusion of 2n gametes: a tetraploid (4n) offspring.
A new species: the 4n plant cannot breed with its 2n parents: speciation in one generation.
